5. The plaintiff possessed the suit land for more than 12 years and acquired indefeasible title, with the whole sale acquisition under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 of the superior interest of the holding by the government the plaintiff became Malik directly under the government by operation of law. 

 6. After death of Anor Ali, defendant No. 1 to 10 started putting various obstacles in the enjoyment of the suit land. Under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, a holding being SA Khatian No. 331 was however, prepared in the name of both the plaintiff and defendant No.1 to 10 taking advantage of such wrong record of rights, defendant No. 1 to 10 started holding out threat to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land. Hence, the suit. 

 7. Defendant No. 4 to 6 only contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. 

 20. The Court of appeal below however reversed the findings on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary on record and found that the Kabuliyat was acted upon. It accordingly held that Anor Ali settled the suit land with the plaintiff as Koal raiyot and after wholesale acquisition such under raiyot became raiyot under the government.
